summary: Proxy Mobile IPv6 requires the mobile access gateway to send a Proxy Binding Update per session to extend its lifetime. This RFC adds group-scoped signaling so many sessions can be refreshed with fewer messages.

plainLanguage.summary: Instead of renewing each ticket one by one, this renews a whole batch with one message.

questions: what is bulk binding update in pmipv6
what is the mobile node group identifier option
what is all-sessions in proxy mobile ipv6
subtitle: Refresh a whole group of Proxy Mobile IPv6 sessions with one message instead of one message per session.

tldr.problem: In Proxy Mobile IPv6, the mobile access gateway must send a separate Proxy Binding Update for every mobility session to extend its lifetime. With millions of sessions on one anchor, that periodic signaling wastes processing power and bandwidth.
tldr.mechanism: The gateway and the anchor exchange group identifiers when a session is created. After that, either side can name a group in a single Proxy Binding Update or Binding Revocation Indication to extend or revoke every session in the group.
tldr.outcome: One message can now refresh or revoke many sessions. Per-session operations still work, and the anchor may decline to enable grouping for a session.

today: RFC 6602 is a Proposed Standard, and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It builds on RFC 5213, RFC 5844 and RFC 5846.

sections.title: Why Group Operations Are Needed
sections.content:
Proxy Mobile IPv6 (RFC 5213) uses a mobile access gateway (MAG) that signals on behalf of each mobile node to a local mobility anchor (LMA). To keep a mobility session alive, the MAG sends a Proxy Binding Update (PBU) to the LMA for each session, even when nothing about the session has changed.

The RFC notes that an LMA can host sessions in the order of a few millions. As that number grows, so does the periodic binding update traffic, and the RFC calls the per-session approach inefficient or sub-optimal in processing power and network bandwidth at both peers.

The base protocol cannot do better because its messages always carry a Mobile Node Identifier option, which limits each operation to a single session. This document adds a group identifier so one message can cover many sessions. Existing single-session behavior is not removed.
sections.plainLanguage: If a school had to send a separate note home for every single student each week, the mailroom would be buried. One note per class is much easier.

sections.title: Bulk Binding Update Groups
sections.content:
A bulk binding update is a binding update operation with group-specific scope. A bulk binding update group is a set of mobility sessions sharing a group identifier. The grouping logic is local to each node, so a session can have two identifiers: one chosen by the MAG and one chosen by the LMA.

The identifiers are exchanged when the session is first created. After that, either peer can operate on a whole group by presenting its own local identifier. The RFC states that the identifier in the option is always the sender's local group, never the peer's. Bulk update is not relevant for creating new sessions.

How a node picks a group is out of scope. The RFC suggests a group might match the service card hosting the session. If no grouping is done, the MAG SHOULD use the default value ALL-SESSIONS, which means all sessions between that LMA and MAG.
sections.plainLanguage: Each side keeps its own seating chart. The teacher has one set of tables and the principal has another, but they swap lists so each can say 'everyone at my table 1'.

sections.title: Flag, Option and Status Code
sections.content:
The RFC adds a Bulk-Binding-Update flag (B) to both the PBU (bit value 0x0040) and the Proxy Binding Acknowledgement, or PBA (bit value 0x08). In a PBU, B=1 asks the LMA to enable bulk support for the session; B=0 means the LMA MUST exclude the session from bulk operations. The flag MUST be 0 when the P flag is 0, and in a PBA it MUST be 0 if the PBU had B=0.

The new Mobile Node Group Identifier option has type 50 and a Length of 6. It carries a Sub-type, a Reserved byte and a 32-bit group identifier. Sub-type 1 is the Bulk Binding Update Group. A message may hold several of these options, each SHOULD have a different sub-type.

The identifier value 0 is reserved and SHOULD NOT be used, and 1 is ALL-SESSIONS. A new PBA status code, INVALID_MOBILE_NODE_GROUP_IDENTIFIER, has the value 175.
sections.plainLanguage: There is a new checkbox on the form saying 'I want group mode', and a new line to write the group number on. A new error message says 'I do not know that group'.

sections.title: Setting Up and Using Groups
sections.content:
When the MAG sends a PBU for a newly attached node, it can set B=1 and include its group identifier in the option. This is a local-policy choice controlled by the variable RequestBulkBindingUpdateSupportForMobilitySession. If the LMA accepts, it assigns its own group (or ALL-SESSIONS), records both identifiers in its Binding Cache entry, and returns B=1 and its identifier in the PBA. The MAG then stores both in its Binding Update List entry. A PBA with B=1 but no option is malformed and ignored. If the PBA is accepted but has B=0, the LMA declined, and the session stays out of bulk operations.

To refresh a group, the MAG sends a PBU with B=0 carrying the group option and none of the single-session identifiers (Mobile Node Identifier, Home Network Prefix, IPv4 Home Address Request or GRE Key options). The LMA extends the lifetime of every session in that MAG's group and answers with status 0, the allocated lifetime, and the group option copied back. An unknown group, or a request that mixes in a session identifier, is rejected with status 175. If the LMA rejects the request administratively, it MUST NOT update any lifetimes.

Revocation works the same way: either peer sends a Binding Revocation Indication (RFC 5846) with the group option and no session identifiers. The receiver revokes every session in the group and replies with a Binding Revocation Acknowledgement. If the indication also carries a session identifier, it is rejected with status 128 (Binding Does NOT Exist).
sections.plainLanguage: Once the groups are agreed, one message saying 'keep group 1 going' keeps everyone in group 1 going, and one message saying 'drop group 2' drops them all at once.

sections.title: Handover, Opt-out and Cleanup
sections.content:
A session can leave bulk mode at any time. A MAG that wants to disable it sends a normal lifetime-extension PBU with B=0 and no group option, then sets both stored identifiers to 0. If the LMA gets a normal PBU with B=0 for a session already in a group, it processes it as usual and treats the 0 as a request to disable bulk support.

When the LMA sees a node move to a new MAG, it SHOULD update the session's group identifier and return the updated identifier in the PBA to the new MAG, but only if the new PBU set B=1. Otherwise the session MUST NOT be placed in any group. When a session is de-registered or revoked for any reason, it MUST be removed from its group.
sections.plainLanguage: If you change schools, you are put in a new class list. If you leave the school, your name comes off every list.

sections.title: Security and IANA
sections.content:
The option itself needs no special security treatment. Group operations are more powerful than single-session ones, though. Without proper authorization checks, a malicious node could hijack a node's session or mount a denial-of-service attack. The RFC therefore requires the LMA to allow only authorized MAGs to perform bulk operations.

IANA allocated the B flag in both the Binding Update Flags and Binding Acknowledgement Flags registries, option type 50, status code 175, and a new Mobile Node Group Identifier Type registry for sub-types. In that registry sub-types 0 and 255 are reserved, 2 through 254 are open, and new values need Expert Review. Two configuration variables, both defaulting to 1, control whether the MAG requests and the LMA accepts bulk support.
sections.plainLanguage: A 'drop the whole class' button is powerful, so only the principal's office is allowed to press it.
